summary: A single Node.js 22 browser-based temperature converter: a stateless HTTP application exposing GET / (HTML page), POST /api/convert (C/F/K conversion with FR4 validation), and GET /health. Conversion logic is isolated in a pure module for server-less unit testing. Zero runtime dependencies; npm test runs node:test assertions, npm run build performs node --check over source, npm start serves on process.env.PORT (default 3000).

tasks.description: Create package.json (CommonJS, Node >=22 engines) with scripts: start, test, build; no runtime dependencies; no lockfile (host-generated).

contracts.description: npm start serves on process.env.PORT default 3000; npm test executes meaningful tests; npm run build checks source syntax.
CommonJS module convention; no runtime dependencies to pin.

tasks.description: Implement pure temperature conversion and validation in lib/convert.js: C/F/K conversion with FR3 formulas, same-unit short-circuit after absolute-zero validation, and validation error messages for FR4.

contracts.description: convert(value, from, to) returns { value, unit }; units limited to C|F|K.
Formulas: C = (F-32)*5/9 and K = C+273.15; same-unit preserves value.
Reject missing/nonnumeric/boolean/unsupported units and below-absolute-zero (including same-unit); boundary epsilon tolerance. origin=assumption for the epsilon magnitude (1e-9).

tasks.description: Implement HTTP application lib/app.js: GET / returns HTML page (numeric input, from/to unit selectors, submit button, result, visible error feedback); POST /api/convert maps validation to 400 {error} and success to 200 {value,unit}; GET /health returns 200 {status:ok}.

contracts.description: GET / returns HTML page with numeric input, source/destination unit selectors, submit button, result and visible error feedback.
POST /api/convert returns 200 {value, unit} on success; 400 {error} on invalid input including malformed JSON.
HTTP handler delegates validation/conversion to lib/convert.js (Pure temperature conversion component).

tasks.description: Implement server entry point server.js that creates the app and listens on process.env.PORT (default 3000).

contracts.description: Starts the HTTP server on PORT env var, default 3000.

tasks.description: Write unit tests test/convert.test.js covering conversion formulas, same-unit, boundary absolute-zero tolerance, and all FR4 rejection cases — no server required.

contracts.description: Tests exercise lib/convert.js directly without a running server (NFR1).

tasks.description: Write HTTP route tests test/app.test.js using node:test with an in-process server/listener, covering GET /, POST /api/convert success and failure, malformed JSON, and GET /health.

contracts.description: Tests verify GET /, POST /api/convert (200 and 400 paths), and GET /health responses.

tasks.description: Write README.md documenting install, start, test, build instructions, the API contract, and limitations (stateless, no persistence, no rounding, boundary tolerance).

assumptions: CommonJS chosen as the consistent module convention (either is permitted by the design; CommonJS keeps node --check/build tooling straightforward).
Absolute-zero boundary tolerance epsilon is 1e-9 (magnitude not specified; any insignificant float error is acceptable per FR4).
The HTML page performs conversion by POST /api/convert via client-side fetch and renders the JSON result/error inline.
The server listens on 0.0.0.0 so it is reachable when run in containers/remapped ports during acceptance (acceptance remaps public ports without assuming host port equals container port).
No deployment artifacts (Docker/Compose/OpenAPI/gateway) are produced because the scope explicitly excludes them.
conflicts: None. The two input documents are consistent: Architecture_View.md is a component view of the same single-app scope described in Architecture_Documentation.md.

Architecture_View.md labels the conversion component 'Convert' while Architecture_Documentation.md does not name the module; resolved by naming it lib/convert.js (labeling of the file is an assumption, not attributed to the source).
